ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, it is known that $AB=6$, $AC=10$, and $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, with $BD\perp AD$ at point $D$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Find the length of $DE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend $BD$ to meet $AC$ at point $F$.\\
Since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD=\angle FAD$.\\
Since $BD\perp AD$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle ADF=90^\circ$.\\
Hence, $\angle ABD=\angle AFD$.\\
Therefore, $AB=AF$ and $BD=DF$.\\
Hence, $D$ is the midpoint of $BF$.\\
Since $AC=10$ and $AB=6$,\\
it follows that $FC=AC-AF=AC-AB=10-6=4$.\\
Since $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
thus $DE$ is the midline of $\triangle BFC$.\\
Therefore, $DE=\frac{1}{2}FC=\frac{1}{2}\times 4=\boxed{2}$.

Hence, $\angle ABD=\angle AFD$. Therefore, $AB=AF$ and $BD=DF$. Hence, $D$ is the midpoint of $BF$. Since $AC=10$ and $AB=6$, $FC=AC-AF=AC-AB=10-6=4$. Since $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $DE$ is the midline of $\triangle BFC$. Therefore, $DE=\frac{1}{2}FC=\frac{1}{2}\times 4=\boxed{2}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is the upper vertex, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is approximately horizontal; line segments AB, AC, and BC form triangle ABC. Point D is located on line segment AD inside the triangle, and BD and AD have a right-angle mark at D; point E is marked on BC, located near below D. Reasoning: According to the specified method, extend BD past D to intersect AC at F. Because AD bisects ∠BAC, and F is on AC, ∠BAD=∠FAD. Also because BD⊥AD, and F is on line BD, ∠ADB=∠ADF=90°. AD is a common side, therefore △ABD and △AFD are congruent, obtaining AB=AF and BD=DF. Given AB=6, so AF=6; and AC=10, therefore FC=AC−AF=10−6=4. At the same time BD=DF, indicating that D is the midpoint of BF. The problem states that E is the midpoint of BC, so in △BFC, DE connects the midpoints of the two sides BF and BC, and is the midline of the triangle, therefore DE=FC/2=4/2=2.
